[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-013-aspnet-to-react-migration-pattern.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

Many organizations operate large portfolios of ASP.NET Web Forms and MVC applications with server-side rendering, ViewState management, and postback-driven interactions. These applications are fundamentally incompatible with client-side micro-frontend architecture, blocking adoption of Module Federation and independent deployment patterns. Teams cannot achieve micro-frontend benefits without first migrating ASP.NET applications to modern React/Angular frameworks.
page_texts.5:
[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-013-aspnet-to-react-migration-pattern.md#solution-overview]

### Solution Overview

The ASP.NET to React Migration pattern defines a systematic strangler fig approach for incrementally replacing legacy ASP.NET applications with modern React single-page applications (SPAs). The pattern addresses ViewState to React state conversion, Telerik/DevExpress to React component mapping, server-side C# logic migration to TypeScript APIs, and authentication modernization from Forms Authentication to OAuth2/OIDC while maintaining HIPAA compliance throughout the migration.

[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-013-aspnet-to-react-migration-pattern.md#when-to-use]

### When to Use

- **Prerequisite for Micro-Frontends**: Application must migrate to React before micro-frontend decomposition possible
- **ViewState Performance Issues**: Large ViewState payloads (100KB-2MB) degrading user experience
- **Technology Obsolescence**: .NET Framework 4.8.1 end-of-life driving modernization requirements
- **Team Skill Evolution**: Development teams transitioning from ASP.NET to modern JavaScript frameworks
- **Product Integration Requirements**: Applications need embeddable widgets for cross-product integration
- **State-Specific Customization**: Multiple state MMIS implementations requiring shared modern platform

[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-013-aspnet-to-react-migration-pattern.md#benefits]

### Benefits

- **Micro-Frontend Enablement**: React applications can adopt Module Federation for independent deployment
- **Performance Improvement**: Client-side rendering eliminates ViewState overhead and full-page postbacks
- **Developer Productivity**: Modern tooling (VS Code, React DevTools, TypeScript) improves development experience
- **Component Reusability**: React components can be shared across products via npm packages
- **Independent Deployment**: Removes IIS application pool dependencies, enables CDN deployment
- **Framework Modernization**: Aligns with widely-adopted industry standards for JavaScript frontend development

[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-013-aspnet-to-react-migration-pattern.md#business-context]

### Business Context

**PRIMARY BLOCKER IDENTIFIED**: Many state MMIS applications use ASP.NET Web Forms/MVC architecture fundamentally incompatible with client-side micro-frontends. Server-side rendering with ViewState prevents JavaScript runtime composition required for Module Federation.

**Business Requirements:**
- **Micro-Frontend Prerequisites**: Must complete ASP.NET → React migration before micro-frontend adoption
- **Migration Scope**: Each major application requires a dedicated migration effort; see PTN-APP-MFE-004 and PTN-APP-MFE-007 for prerequisite infrastructure
- **State Implementations**: Multiple state Medicaid systems require unified modern platform
- **Product Integration**: Enterprise™, Provider+™, Whole Health™, Connect™ need embeddable widgets
- **Regulatory Compliance**: Maintain HIPAA, Section 508 compliance throughout migration

**Affected Applications:**
- **Enterprise™ (MMIS)**: Multiple state implementations with varying .NET Framework versions (2.0-4.8.1)
- **Provider+™**: Provider enrollment and credentialing applications
- **Whole Health™**: Care coordination and population health applications
- **Connect™**: Integration monitoring and FHIR API management dashboards
- **State-Specific Customizations**: Divergent Telerik/DevExpress versions per state

[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-013-aspnet-to-react-migration-pattern.md#technical-context]

### Technical Context

**Current ASP.NET Technology Stack:**
- **Frameworks**: ASP.NET Web Forms (.NET Framework 2.0-4.8.1), ASP.NET MVC (Razor views)
- **Component Libraries**: Telerik UI for ASP.NET AJAX (2025.x), DevExpress ASP.NET (22.x-24.x)
- **State Management**: ViewState (100KB-2MB payloads), Session State, Application State
- **Routing**: Page-based routing (`.aspx`), MVC convention-based routing
- **Authentication**: ASP.NET Forms Authentication, Windows Authentication, custom membership providers
- **Deployment**: IIS (Internet Information Services), coordinated application pool recycles

**Target React Technology Stack:**
- **Framework**: React 18+ with TypeScript 5+
- **State Management**: React Context, Redux Toolkit, or Zustand
- **Component Library**: Custom React design system replacing Telerik/DevExpress
- **Routing**: React Router 6+
- **Authentication**: OAuth2/OIDC with PKCE flow
- **Build Tools**: Vite or Webpack 5 with Module Federation
- **Deployment**: CDN (AWS CloudFront, Azure CDN) with containerized backend APIs

**Modern Build Infrastructure Already Exists:**
- Care Management applications successfully use React 18/Angular 14/Webpack/npm
- Proves Gainwell has operational modern JavaScript build infrastructure
- ASP.NET migrations can leverage existing Care Management tooling and practices

[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-013-aspnet-to-react-migration-pattern.md#problem-details]

### Problem Details

**Problem 1: ViewState Architecture Incompatibility**

ASP.NET Web Forms uses server-side ViewState stored in hidden fields, sent with every postback:

```html
<!-- ViewState can be 100KB-2MB per page -->
<input type="hidden" name="__VIEWSTATE" value="..." />
```

**Impact:**
- Cannot decompose into micro-frontends—ViewState requires full page context
- Poor performance on slow connections (ViewState sent with every request)
- Server-side session affinity prevents horizontal scaling

**Problem 2: Telerik/DevExpress Server Control Lock-in**

Components are ASP.NET server controls, not reusable in React:

```aspx
<%-- Telerik server control - cannot export to React/npm --%>
<telerik:RadGrid ID="ClaimsGrid" runat="server"
    OnNeedDataSource="ClaimsGrid_NeedDataSource">
</telerik:RadGrid>
```

**Impact:**
- Must rebuild all healthcare-specific widgets in React
- $320K-$480K estimated cost for design system development
- 16-24 weeks timeline for component library

**Problem 3: C# Server-Side Business Logic**

Business logic embedded in code-behind files:

```csharp
// Code-behind (.aspx.cs) - must migrate to TypeScript + API
protected void SubmitClaim_Click(object sender, EventArgs e) {
    var claim = new Claim {
        MemberId = txtMemberId.Text,
        Amount = decimal.Parse(txtAmount.Text)
    };
    claimService.ProcessClaim(claim);
    Response.Redirect("ClaimConfirmation.aspx");
}
```

**Impact:**
- Cannot reuse server-side C# logic in React
- Must refactor to RESTful APIs with TypeScript/C# backend
- Risk of business logic divergence during migration

[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-013-aspnet-to-react-migration-pattern.md#forces-and-constraints]

### Forces and Constraints

**Constraints:**
- **Live Production Systems**: Cannot take applications offline during migration
- **State Contract Obligations**: Must maintain SLA commitments during transition
- **HIPAA Compliance**: PHI protection required throughout migration
- **Section 508 Accessibility**: Must maintain WCAG 2.2 AA compliance
- **Budget Limitations**: $2.4M-$4.8M per application budget constraints
- **Timeline Pressure**: 12-24 months per major application target

**Competing Forces:**
- **Speed vs. Quality**: Faster migration risks technical debt accumulation
- **Big Bang vs. Incremental**: Complete rewrites faster but riskier than strangler fig
- **Reuse vs. Rebuild**: Porting legacy patterns faster but carries forward debt
- **Team Capacity**: Existing teams maintain legacy while building new React applications

[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-013-aspnet-to-react-migration-pattern.md#pattern-description]

### Pattern Description

The ASP.NET to React Migration pattern employs a **strangler fig approach** where new React features incrementally replace ASP.NET pages until the legacy application is fully retired. The pattern consists of:

1. **Dual Runtime Coexistence**: Run ASP.NET (IIS) and React (CDN) simultaneously with routing layer
2. **Incremental Page Migration**: Replace ASP.NET pages one-by-one with React routes
3. **API Extraction**: Extract C# business logic to RESTful APIs consumed by React
4. **Component Library Development**: Build React design system replacing Telerik/DevExpress
5. **Authentication Bridge**: Implement shared authentication between ASP.NET and React
6. **Data Migration**: Migrate ViewState/Session State to React client-side or backend APIs
7. **Testing Parallel**: Run automated tests against both ASP.NET and React during transition
8. **Cutover Strategy**: Gradually route traffic from ASP.NET to React until 100% migrated

[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-013-aspnet-to-react-migration-pattern.md#components]

### Components

| Component | Responsibility | Dependencies |
|-----------|---------------|--------------|
| **Routing Layer** | Routes traffic between ASP.NET and React based on feature flags | Nginx, CloudFront, feature toggle service |
| **React Application** | New SPA replacing ASP.NET pages incrementally | React 18+, TypeScript, React Router |
| **Backend APIs** | RESTful APIs extracted from C# business logic | ASP.NET Core Web API, Entity Framework Core |
| **Authentication Bridge** | Shared auth between ASP.NET Forms Auth and OAuth2 | IdentityServer4, cookie sharing middleware |
| **Design System (React)** | Component library replacing Telerik/DevExpress | React 18+, Storybook, styled-components |
| **Legacy ASP.NET App** | Existing application gradually deprecated | IIS, .NET Framework, ViewState |
| **Shared Data Layer** | Database accessed by both ASP.NET and React APIs | SQL Server, Entity Framework, Dapper |

[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-013-aspnet-to-react-migration-pattern.md#interactions]

### Interactions

**User Request Flow During Migration:**

1. User navigates to `/claims/search`
2. Routing Layer checks feature flag: is `/claims/search` migrated to React?
3. **If React**: Route to CloudFront → React SPA → Backend API
4. **If ASP.NET**: Route to IIS → ASP.NET page with ViewState
5. Authentication token shared via httpOnly cookie accessible to both runtimes
6. React SPA calls RESTful API for data; ASP.NET page uses ADO.NET/Entity Framework
7. Both runtimes log to centralized observability platform (Datadog, Application Insights)

[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-013-aspnet-to-react-migration-pattern.md#variations]

### Variations

**Variation 1: Big Bang Rewrite** (Not Recommended)
- Rebuild entire application in React before deploying
- Pros: Clean slate, no dual runtime complexity
- Cons: High risk, long time without production deployments, difficult to validate

**Variation 2: Incremental Page-by-Page** (Recommended)
- Migrate one page/route at a time from ASP.NET to React
- Pros: Continuous production deployments, lower risk, easier rollback
- Cons: Dual runtime overhead, routing complexity

**Variation 3: Subdomain Split**
- Deploy React app on separate subdomain (new.enterprise.gainwell.com)
- Pros: Clear separation, independent deployments
- Cons: SSO complexity, user confusion, cannot share routes

### Prerequisites

**Organizational Readiness:**
- Executive sponsorship acknowledging $2.4M-$4.8M investment per application
- 12-24 month timeline commitment without scope creep pressure
- Development team training in React/TypeScript (4-8 weeks ramp-up)
- Product owner availability for requirements refinement

**Technical Prerequisites:**

- CDN infrastructure provisioned (CloudFront, Akamai, Azure CDN)
- Backend API platform selected (ASP.NET Core Web API recommended)
- Design system foundation started (Storybook, component architecture)
- Authentication modernization plan (OAuth2/OIDC migration strategy)

**Team Composition:**
- 1 Solution Architect (React + ASP.NET expertise)
- 2-3 Senior React Developers (TypeScript, hooks, performance optimization)
- 2-3 Full-Stack Developers (C# backend API development)
- 1 UI/UX Designer (healthcare domain experience)
- 1 QA Engineer (Playwright/Cypress automation)
- 1 DevOps Engineer (CDN, CI/CD pipeline setup)

[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-013-aspnet-to-react-migration-pattern.md#phase-1-foundation-months-1-3]

#### Phase 1: Foundation (Months 1-3)

1. **Establish Dual Runtime Architecture**
   - Deploy Nginx/CloudFront routing layer with feature toggle integration
   - Configure ASP.NET and React to share authentication cookies
   - Set up monitoring and observability for both runtimes
   - Implement A/B testing infrastructure for gradual rollout

2. **Develop React Design System Foundation**
   - Inventory Telerik/DevExpress components used across application
   - Design React component API contracts (props, events, accessibility)
   - Implement 20-30 core components (Button, Input, Table, Modal, etc.)
   - Set up Storybook documentation with healthcare examples
   - Establish accessibility testing pipeline (axe-core, pa11y)

3. **Extract First Backend API**
   - Select low-risk page for pilot migration (e.g., static reference data page)
   - Extract C# business logic to ASP.NET Core Web API endpoint
   - Implement API versioning, error handling, logging
   - Add Swagger/OpenAPI documentation
   - Write integration tests validating API behavior

4. **Migrate Pilot Page to React**
   - Build React component tree replacing ASP.NET page
   - Integrate with backend API for data fetching
   - Implement form validation matching legacy behavior
   - Add Playwright E2E tests validating workflows
   - Deploy behind feature flag (5% traffic)
page_texts.24:
[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-013-aspnet-to-react-migration-pattern.md#phase-2-acceleration-months-4-9]

#### Phase 2: Acceleration (Months 4-9)

1. **Scale Component Library**
   - Build healthcare-specific components (Member Card, Claim Grid, Provider Listing)
   - Implement data visualization components (Charts, Dashboards)
   - Add form builder patterns for complex workflows
   - Establish npm publishing pipeline for component reuse

2. **Migrate High-Value Pages**
   - Prioritize pages by business value and migration complexity
   - Target 2-3 pages per 2-week sprint
   - Extract backend APIs in parallel with React development
   - Gradually increase React traffic percentage (25% → 50% → 75%)

3. **Authentication Modernization**
   - Migrate from ASP.NET Forms Authentication to OAuth2/OIDC
   - Implement PKCE flow for React SPA
   - Configure IdentityServer4 or Azure AD B2C
   - Maintain session timeout enforcement (HIPAA 15-minute requirement)

4. **Data Migration Strategy**
   - Eliminate ViewState dependencies by moving state to client or APIs
   - Replace Session State with JWT tokens or Redis cache
   - Refactor Application State to environment configuration
page_texts.25:
[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-013-aspnet-to-react-migration-pattern.md#phase-3-completion-months-10-18]

#### Phase 3: Completion (Months 10-18)

1. **Migrate Remaining Pages**
   - Complete migration of all ASP.NET pages to React
   - Route 100% traffic to React application
   - Keep ASP.NET runtime in read-only mode for 30-60 days (rollback safety)

2. **Decommission Legacy ASP.NET**
   - Archive ASP.NET codebase for compliance retention
   - Terminate IIS infrastructure
   - Cancel Telerik/DevExpress licenses ($2K-$5K/developer savings)
   - Document lessons learned and migration patterns

3. **Micro-Frontend Preparation**
   - Application now ready for micro-frontend decomposition
   - Implement Module Federation for independent deployment
   - Begin breaking React monolith into domain-aligned modules

[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-013-aspnet-to-react-migration-pattern.md#best-practices]

### Best Practices

- **Start with Low-Risk Pages**: Migrate static content pages before complex workflows
- **Maintain Feature Parity**: React version must match ASP.NET behavior exactly initially
- **Automated Testing**: Write Playwright E2E tests before migration to validate behavior
- **Incremental Traffic Rollout**: Use feature flags for gradual traffic shifting (5% → 25% → 50% → 100%)
- **Performance Budgets**: New React pages must load faster than ASP.NET equivalents
- **Accessibility First**: Run axe-core on every React component before production
- **API-First Development**: Extract APIs before building React UI to validate contracts
- **Component Reusability**: Build components with reuse across products in mind
- **HIPAA Audit Logging**: Maintain PHI access logging throughout migration
page_texts.31:
[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-013-aspnet-to-react-migration-pattern.md#common-pitfalls]

### Common Pitfalls

- **Pitfall 1: Big Bang Rewrite Temptation**
  - **Issue**: Attempting complete rewrite instead of incremental migration
  - **Impact**: 12-18 months without production deployments, high risk
  - **Solution**: Use strangler fig pattern with bi-weekly production releases

- **Pitfall 2: Skipping API Extraction**
  - **Issue**: Porting C# business logic directly to TypeScript in React components
  - **Impact**: Business logic duplication, cannot reuse across products, testing complexity
  - **Solution**: Extract all business logic to backend APIs first, then build React UI

- **Pitfall 3: ViewState Dependencies**
  - **Issue**: React components trying to replicate ViewState behavior
  - **Impact**: Client-side state bloat, performance degradation
  - **Solution**: Eliminate ViewState entirely—use backend APIs or client-side state management

- **Pitfall 4: Component Library Scope Creep**
  - **Issue**: Building overly generic component library delaying migrations
  - **Impact**: 6-12 month design system development blocking page migrations
  - **Solution**: Build components just-in-time as needed for migrations (20-30 core components sufficient to start)

- **Pitfall 5: Authentication Migration Delay**
  - **Issue**: Deferring OAuth2/OIDC migration until late in project
  - **Impact**: Security vulnerabilities, SSO complexity, rollback difficulties
  - **Solution**: Migrate authentication in Phase 1 foundation (Months 1-3)

[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-013-aspnet-to-react-migration-pattern.md#compliance-requirements]

### Compliance Requirements

**HIPAA Compliance:**
- Maintain PHI access audit logging throughout migration
- Encrypt PHI in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest
- Implement session timeout enforcement (15-minute requirement)
- Document security controls in System Security Plan (SSP)

**Section 508 Accessibility:**
- All React components must pass axe-core automated testing
- Manual keyboard navigation testing required before production
- Screen reader compatibility validation (JAWS, NVDA)
- Color contrast ratios meet WCAG 2.2 AA (4.5:1 for normal text)

**State Contract Obligations:**
- Maintain SLA commitments during migration (99.5% uptime typical)
- Provide 30-60 day notice for major UI changes to state users
- Offer user training and documentation for new React interface
- Maintain legacy ASP.NET in read-only mode for 30-60 days post-cutover

[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-013-aspnet-to-react-migration-pattern.md#real-world-example-1-state-mmis-claims-search-migration]

### Real-World Example 1: State MMIS Claims Search Migration

**Context:**
State of Ohio Enterprise™ MMIS claims search page—high-traffic page (10K+ daily users) with complex Telerik RadGrid, 500KB ViewState payload, 3-5 second page loads.

**Implementation:**
1. Extracted claims search API from ASP.NET code-behind to ASP.NET Core Web API (2 weeks)
2. Built React claims search component with virtualized table for performance (3 weeks)
3. Added Playwright E2E tests validating 20 search scenarios (1 week)
4. Deployed behind feature flag, gradually increased traffic: 5% (week 1) → 25% (week 3) → 50% (week 5) → 100% (week 7)
5. Monitored performance: Initial page load reduced from 3-5s to <1.5s, ViewState eliminated

**Outcome:**
- 60% performance improvement (3-5s → <1.5s page loads)
- User satisfaction increased from 72% to 91% (post-migration survey)
- Eliminated 500KB ViewState reducing bandwidth costs by $15K/month
- React component reused across 8 other state implementations
page_texts.39:
[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-013-aspnet-to-react-migration-pattern.md#real-world-example-2-provider-enrollment-form-migration]

### Real-World Example 2: Provider+™ Enrollment Form Migration

**Context:**
Provider enrollment form—40+ fields with complex validation, Telerik RadAsyncUpload for documents, ViewState 1.2MB, accessibility issues reported by state users.

**Implementation:**
1. Rebuilt form using React Hook Form + Zod validation (4 weeks)
2. Replaced Telerik file upload with React Dropzone (WCAG 2.2 AA compliant)
3. Extracted validation logic to shared npm package for reuse
4. Added axe-core automated testing catching 15 accessibility issues
5. Migrated 10% of states initially, resolved issues, then scaled to 100%

**Outcome:**
- ViewState eliminated (1.2MB → 0KB)
- Accessibility compliance achieved (0 axe-core violations)
- Form submission success rate increased from 87% to 96% (better validation UX)
- Validation logic reused across 4 other forms in Provider+™ and Enterprise™

[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-013-aspnet-to-react-migration-pattern.md#scenario-1-high-traffic-member-portal]

#### Scenario 1: High-Traffic Member Portal

**When to Use:** Public-facing member portal with 100K+ monthly users, high performance requirements

**Approach:**
- Start with static pages (FAQs, contact info) for low-risk pilot
- Migrate member authentication and profile pages next (critical path)
- Tackle complex workflows (claims lookup, document upload) in Phase 2
- Use CDN caching aggressively (CloudFront) for static assets
- Implement service workers for offline functionality

#### Scenario 2: Internal Care Coordination Dashboard

**When to Use:** Internal staff application with complex data visualizations, lower traffic but higher complexity

**Approach:**
- Migrate dashboards and reporting pages early (high value, moderate complexity)
- Build custom chart components in design system (reuse across products)
- Extract analytics APIs to backend services for caching
- Implement real-time data updates using WebSockets or Server-Sent Events
- Focus on keyboard navigation for power users

[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-013-aspnet-to-react-migration-pattern.md#scenario-3-state-specific-customization]

#### Scenario 3: State-Specific Customization

**When to Use:** Multiple state implementations with varying Medicaid program rules

**Approach:**
- Establish common React platform first (shared components, routing, auth)
- Implement state-specific logic via configuration/feature flags, not code forks
- Use React component composition for state customization (slot patterns)
- Maintain single codebase with configuration-driven customization
- Migrate one pilot state first, validate approach, then scale to others

[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-013-aspnet-to-react-migration-pattern.md#before-aspnet-web-forms]

#### Before (ASP.NET Web Forms)

```text
User Experience:

- Page loads: 3-5 seconds (ViewState overhead)
- Full page postbacks on every interaction
- Loss of scroll position after postback
- Limited client-side validation (server roundtrip required)

Developer Experience:

- 10-25 minute build times (Visual Studio solution)
- Difficult to test (requires IIS, SQL Server)
- C# code-behind tightly coupled to UI
- Limited component reusability across products

Performance:

- 500KB-1.2MB ViewState payloads
- Full page rendering on every postback
- Server-side session affinity required
- Limited CDN usage (server-rendered content)

Deployment:

- IIS application pool recycles (30-60s downtime)
- Coordinated releases across teams
- 2-4 deployments per week
- Difficult rollback (database schema dependencies)
```

[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-013-aspnet-to-react-migration-pattern.md#tldr]

## TL;DR

**Problem:** ASP.NET Web Forms/MVC applications use server-side rendering with ViewState, fundamentally incompatible with client-side micro-frontends. Must migrate to React before micro-frontend architecture becomes possible.

**Solution:** Strangler fig migration pattern where React pages incrementally replace ASP.NET pages. Run dual runtime (IIS + React CDN) with routing layer directing traffic based on feature flags. Extract C# business logic to backend APIs, build React component library replacing Telerik/DevExpress, modernize authentication to OAuth2/OIDC.

**When to Use:**
- Prerequisite for micro-frontend adoption
- ViewState performance issues (100KB-2MB payloads)
- .NET Framework 4.8.1 end-of-life driving modernization
- Product integration requiring embeddable React widgets

**Key Benefits:**
- **Micro-Frontend Enablement**: React applications can adopt Module Federation
- **60% Performance Improvement**: Eliminates ViewState overhead and postbacks
- **Independent Deployment**: Removes IIS dependencies, enables CDN deployment

**Implementation Complexity:** **High** (12-24 months, $2.4M-$4.8M per application)

**Prerequisites:** Modern build infrastructure (Node.js, Webpack - already exists via Care Management), CDN provisioned, team trained in React/TypeScript (4-8 weeks), executive sponsorship for budget and timeline

**Related Patterns:** [Build Infrastructure](./PTN-APP-MFE-007-pattern.md) | [Design System](./PTN-APP-MFE-005-pattern.md) | [Authentication](./PTN-APP-MFE-001-pattern.md) | [Module Composition](./PTN-APP-MFE-003-pattern.md)
